source_caption:
The shower scene in Psycho became legendary because Alfred Hitchcock created terror through editing rather than explicit violence. The sequence uses dozens of rapid cuts, Bernard Herrmann’s stabbing strings, and Janet Leigh’s terrified performance to make viewers feel like they saw more than they actually did — changing horror cinema forever.

Psycho (1960), directed by Alfred Hitchcock, starring Anthony Perkins, Janet Leigh, Vera Miles. A groundbreaking psychological horror film that turns an ordinary motel stop into a nightmare of suspense, identity, and obsession.

source_details.synopsis: Psycho is a 1960 American horror thriller film produced and directed by Alfred Hitchcock. The screenplay, written by Joseph Stefano, is based on the 1959 novel by Robert Bloch. The film stars Anthony Perkins, Janet Leigh, Vera Miles, John Gavin, and Martin Balsam. The plot centers on an encounter between on-the-run embezzler Marion Crane (Leigh), shy motel proprietor Norman Bates (Perkins), and his disturbed mother. A private investigator (Balsam), Marion's lover Sam Loomis (Gavin), and her sister Lila (Miles) investigate Marion's subsequent disappearance.
